rows.question: What does low oil pressure usually mean?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature
rows.answer: Oil pressure is the pressure the oil pump creates to push oil through the bearings, camshaft and other moving parts. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure] Pressure is lowest at hot idle and rises with RPM. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure] Low oil pressure is one of the most serious warnings an engine gives: it can mean the oil level is low, the oil is too thin or degraded, the oil filter or pickup is blocked, the pump is worn, or the bearings are worn. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure]

rows.question: The oil pressure warning light came on while driving. What should I do?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
AutoCare sensor glossary: Reading an AutoCare risk score
AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature
rows.answer: Oil pressure is the pressure the oil pump creates to push oil through the bearings, camshaft and other moving parts. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure] Pressure is lowest at hot idle and rises with RPM. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure] If the oil pressure warning light comes on while driving, stop the engine as soon as it is safe and check the oil level; driving on with no oil pressure can destroy the engine within minutes. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure]

rows.question: Why would oil pressure be too high?

[AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure] Unusually high oil pressure can come from oil that is too thick, a stuck pressure-relief valve or a blocked passage. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure]

rows.question: What causes an engine to overheat?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Oil versus coolant temperature
rows.answer: Low coolant pressure can mean a leak, a faulty cap or low coolant level; the engine may then overheat. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] Never open the radiator or expansion-tank cap while the engine is hot: the coolant can spray out and scald. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] A reading that climbs above normal means the engine is overheating; likely causes are low coolant, a leak, a thermostat stuck closed, a failed water pump, a blocked radiator or a cooling fan that does not switch on. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant temperature]

rows.question: The temperature warning light is on. What should I do first?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Oil versus coolant temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Reading an AutoCare risk score
rows.answer: Coolant temperature is the engine's main health gauge. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant temperature] If the temperature warning light comes on, stop when safe, switch off the engine and let it cool before checking the coolant level. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant temperature] Oil temperature shows how hot the engine oil is. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature]

[AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant temperature] Oil and coolant temperatures normally rise together and settle close to each other once the engine is warm. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Oil versus coolant temperature]

rows.answer: Never open the radiator or expansion-tank cap while the engine is hot: the coolant can spray out and scald. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] A reading that climbs above normal means the engine is overheating; likely causes are low coolant, a leak, a thermostat stuck closed, a failed water pump, a blocked radiator or a cooling fan that does not switch on. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant temperature] If the temperature warning light comes on, stop when safe, switch off the engine and let it cool before checking the coolant level. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant temperature]

rows.question: What does low coolant pressure indicate?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: The cooling system runs under pressure so the coolant can get hotter than its normal boiling point without boiling. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] Low coolant pressure can mean a leak, a faulty cap or low coolant level; the engine may then overheat. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] Pressure that rises quickly, or bubbles in the expansion tank, can indicate combustion gas entering the coolant, which is a sign of a failing head gasket. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure]

rows.question: Bubbles in the expansion tank: what could that mean?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: The radiator or expansion-tank cap holds that pressure. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] Pressure that rises quickly, or bubbles in the expansion tank, can indicate combustion gas entering the coolant, which is a sign of a failing head gasket. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] Never open the radiator or expansion-tank cap while the engine is hot: the coolant can spray out and scald. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure]

rows.question: Why is the cooling system pressurised?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Oil versus coolant temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature
rows.answer: The cooling system runs under pressure so the coolant can get hotter than its normal boiling point without boiling. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] The radiator or expansion-tank cap holds that pressure. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant pressure] A reading that climbs above normal means the engine is overheating; likely causes are low coolant, a leak, a thermostat stuck closed, a failed water pump, a blocked radiator or a cooling fan that does not switch on. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Coolant temperature]

rows.question: What are symptoms of low fuel pressure?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: Fuel pressure is the pressure the fuel pump supplies to the injectors. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Too little pressure starves the engine: symptoms include hard starting, hesitation under load, misfires and loss of power. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Common causes are a weak fuel pump, a clogged fuel filter, a faulty pressure regulator or a leak. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure]

rows.question: What happens if fuel pressure is too high?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: Fuel pressure is the pressure the fuel pump supplies to the injectors. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Common causes are a weak fuel pump, a clogged fuel filter, a faulty pressure regulator or a leak. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Too much pressure makes the mixture rich, which can cause poor fuel economy, black smoke and fouled spark plugs; a stuck regulator or a blocked return line are typical causes. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure]

rows.question: I can smell fuel near the engine. Is that dangerous?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: Fuel pressure is the pressure the fuel pump supplies to the injectors. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Too little pressure starves the engine: symptoms include hard starting, hesitation under load, misfires and loss of power. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Any smell of fuel or visible fuel leak is a fire risk and needs a mechanic before the vehicle is driven. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure]

rows.question: Could a clogged fuel filter cause hesitation under load?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: Too little pressure starves the engine: symptoms include hard starting, hesitation under load, misfires and loss of power. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Common causes are a weak fuel pump, a clogged fuel filter, a faulty pressure regulator or a leak. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure] Too much pressure makes the mixture rich, which can cause poor fuel economy, black smoke and fouled spark plugs; a stuck regulator or a blocked return line are typical causes. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Fuel pressure]

rows.question: Why does oil temperature run hotter than normal?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Oil versus coolant temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: Oil temperature shows how hot the engine oil is. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature] Oil that runs hotter than usual thins out and protects the engine less, and it ages faster. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature] High oil temperature often follows from cooling problems, heavy load or towing, a low oil level, or an oil cooler that is blocked. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature]

rows.question: Is it bad if the oil never gets warm on short trips?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Oil versus coolant temperature
AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil pressure
rows.answer: Oil temperature shows how hot the engine oil is. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature] Oil that stays cold for a long time, for example on very short trips, does not burn off moisture and fuel, which also degrades it. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Lubricant oil temperature] Oil and coolant temperatures normally rise together and settle close to each other once the engine is warm. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Oil versus coolant temperature]

rows.question: My idle speed keeps hunting up and down. What causes that?
rows.answer: At idle a warm petrol engine usually turns slowly and steadily; RPM rises with throttle. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Engine RPM] An idle that hunts up and down, or that is much higher than usual once the engine is warm, can point to a vacuum leak, a dirty throttle body, a faulty idle control or a sensor fault. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Engine RPM] Very low RPM together with low oil pressure is a common pattern in readings from engines that need attention, because oil pump output falls with engine speed. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Engine RPM]

rows.question: Is the AutoCare risk score the same as a mechanic's inspection?
retrieved: AutoCare sensor glossary: Reading an AutoCare risk score
rows.answer: The AutoCare fault-risk score is a statistical estimate from a model trained on snapshot sensor readings. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Reading an AutoCare risk score] It is not an inspection and it cannot see wear, leaks or noises. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Reading an AutoCare risk score] Treat a high score as a prompt to check the readings it highlights, starting with oil level and coolant level, and have a qualified mechanic inspect the engine before relying on the vehicle. [AutoCare sensor glossary: Reading an AutoCare risk score]
